per_dimension.notes: Two multi-query actor-matching concepts appear: (1) ELN identification; (2) FARC dissidents (EMC) mapping. They use different name/alias predicates across queries, leading to different row sets.

Corridor regions are defined inconsistently (municipality subset vs entire departments). There are also diacritic (accent) inconsistencies for municipality names like Cúcuta that affect equality filters.
Most 2022–2024 and 2023–2024 windows are applied consistently. One ELN time window differs (2022-07-01 vs 2022-08-07) across queries.
Definitions for Explosions/Remote subtypes (IED, Shelling, Air/drone) and VAC Attack are consistently filtered where used.
Actor fatality attribution at municipality level uses incompatible methods across queries (single-side vs dual-side attribution), changing top-actor and shares.
One 2024 lethality query omits the country filter entirely. Municipal concentration queries differ on including only political-violence disorder types vs all events.

conflicts.predicate_a: Q13: (actor1 ILIKE '%ELN%' OR actor2 ILIKE '%ELN%' OR assoc_actor_1 ILIKE '%ELN%' OR assoc_actor_2 ILIKE '%ELN%')
conflicts.predicate_b: Q31: (actor1 ILIKE '%ELN%' OR actor2 ILIKE '%ELN%' OR assoc_actor_1 ILIKE '%ELN%' OR assoc_actor_2 ILIKE '%ELN%' OR actor1/2/assoc ILIKE '%Ejercito de Liberacion Nacional%' OR '%National Liberation Army%')
conflicts.explanation: Q13 misses events labeled only with Spanish/English full names (without 'ELN' substring), while Q31 includes them. This changes ELN event totals and lethality metrics.

conflicts.predicate_a: Q12: CASE mapping to 'FARC-EMC' using ILIKEs for 'Estado Mayor Central', 'FARC-EMC', 'FARC EP (EMC)', 'EMC FARC', 'FARC%Estado Mayor Central%' plus NOT-exclusions (truncated).
conflicts.predicate_b: Q19: CASE mapping to 'FARC dissidents - EMC' using patterns like 'FARC dissidents: Estado Mayor Central%', '%Estado Mayor Central%', and named fronts (Dagoberto Ramos, Jaime Martínez, Carlos Patiño).
conflicts.explanation: Different alias sets and pattern anchors mean some fronts/labels will be included in one mapping but not the other, altering counts attributed to EMC.

conflicts.explanation: Different start dates include/exclude several weeks of events; any trend or level comparisons will differ.

conflicts.predicate_b: Q26: actor_attrib uses COALESCE(actor1, actor2) to choose a single actor per event for attribution.
conflicts.explanation: These attribution schemes yield different top actors and different shares of municipal fatalities; Q25 may over-attribute by double counting fatalities.

conflicts.predicate_b: Q9: WHERE country = 'Colombia' AND year = 2024 AND event_type = 'Battles' or 'Explosions/Remote violence'.
conflicts.explanation: Q4 aggregates globally, not just Colombia, producing vastly different percentiles and top-shares; these cannot be compared to Colombia-only results elsewhere.

conflicts.predicate_b: Q23: WHERE country='Colombia' AND year=2024 (no disorder_type filter)
conflicts.explanation: Q23 may include non-political-violence event types, inflating totals and altering shares/HHI vs the political-violence-only scope in Q22.

summary: The queries contain several result-changing inconsistencies, notably in actor matching (ELN and FARC-EMC aliases), corridor geography definitions (municipality subset vs whole departments and accent usage), differing ELN time windows, a missing country filter in a key 2024 lethality query, and incompatible actor-attribution methods at the municipality level. Event taxonomy filters are generally consistent, and most year-window filters align, but the above issues undermine cross-query comparability.
